title: Woodhouse configuration
description: Configuration for the Woodhouse GitHub App. Place at `.github/woodhouse.yml` in a repository, or `woodhouse.yml` in the owner's `.github-private` repository to set an owner-wide baseline.

inherit.description: Set on a repository's local config to opt out of the inherited baseline entirely rather than merging with it.

enabled.description: Master switch. Off by default: installing this app must not silently start rewriting repository settings until it is explicitly asked to.

pruneLabels.description: Remove labels that exist on the repo but are absent from config.

pruneRulesets.description: Converge everything: delete every ruleset in the repository that is not named in this configuration — including rulesets created outside Woodhouse. Off by default. There is no ownership marker to fall back on: GitHub's ruleset API has no metadata slot for one, so prune cannot tell a hand-made ruleset from a managed one. Turn it on only when the ruleset list below is genuinely the whole truth for the repository.

settings.description: Repo-settings sync: the master switch plus the prune toggles for labels and rulesets. Off by default.

allow_auto_merge.description: Allow pull requests to be auto-merged once the requirements pass.

delete_branch_on_merge.description: Delete the head branch automatically once a pull request merges.

allow_update_branch.description: Offer the `Update branch` button on pull requests.

topics.description: Repository topic list. Replaces all topics on the repo; GitHub lowercases them.

repository.description: Repository settings synced when `settings.enabled` is true.

branchProtection.description: Classic branch protection keyed by branch name; every configured branch is PUT wholesale and idempotently on each sync. Fields left unset are omitted from the write (GitHub keeps them as-is), except the three API-required fields (`required_status_checks`, `enforce_admins`, `required_pull_request_reviews`), which are sent as explicit `null` when unset; a branch that does not exist is skipped, not an error.

required_status_checks.description: Status checks a branch must satisfy. API-required null: sent as null when unset; sub-fields left out are kept by GitHub.

strict.description: Require branches to be up to date with the base branch before merging.

contexts.description: Check context names (GitHub Actions workflow/job) that must pass.

enforce_admins.description: Apply branch protections to repository admins too. API-required null: sent as null when unset.

required_pull_request_reviews.description: Pull-request review protections. API-required null: sent as null when unset; sub-fields left out are kept by GitHub.

required_approving_review_count.description: How many approving reviews are required (0-6).

dismiss_stale_reviews.description: Dismiss a review when new commits land.

require_code_owner_reviews.description: Require approval from code owners for their files.

require_last_push_approval.description: A PR must be approved after its last commit.

required_linear_history.description: Only allow commits that extend the branch tip (no merges).

required_conversation_resolution.description: Require all conversations to be resolved before merging.

lock_branch.description: Lock the branch against any pushes.

block_creations.description: Prevent creation of the branch by users without write access.

labels.description: Repository labels converge to this list; removal is governed by `settings.pruneLabels`.

color.description: Colour as six hex digits; a leading `#` is accepted and stripped on apply.

description.description: Label description — at most 100 characters, GitHub's limit.

from.description: Rename an existing label to `name` first.

rulesets.description: Repository rulesets converge to this list; every configured ruleset is re-declared wholesale on every sync (create or update, matched by name — GitHub's GET is too normalised to diff). The perimeter is typed and the core is open: `type` is required (catches obvious mistakes) and the rest of each rule body passes through, GitHub validates on write. Supported rule types as prose (deliberately not an enum — GitHub extends the union regularly), indicative not validation: creation, update, deletion, required_linear_history, merge_queue, required_deployments, required_signatures, pull_request, required_status_checks, non_fast_forward, commit_message_pattern, commit_author_email_pattern, committer_email_pattern, branch_name_pattern, tag_name_pattern, workflows, code_scanning, code_quality, code_coverage, copilot_code_review, license_compliance_scanning, file_path_restriction, max_file_path_length, file_extension_restriction, max_file_size. `secret_scanning` is documented but absent from the REST array. Conditions accept only `ref_name` (organization-level keys 422 on this endpoint, rejected at authoring time instead of mid-sync). WARN: `settings.pruneRulesets` deletes every ruleset not named here, including hand-made ones.

name.description: Ruleset name. The case-insensitive match key for updates, deletes, and prune protection — two rulesets differing only in case are rejected as a collision at authoring time.

target.description: What the ruleset applies to: branch, tag, or push.

enforcement.description: active enforces; evaluate monitors without blocking; disabled is a no-op.

bypass_actors.description: Actors allowed to bypass this ruleset. actor_type selects the kind, actor_id names the specific actor, bypass_mode controls scope (mirrors the REST reference).

actor_id.description: The specific actor's ID (user, team, org role, deploy key, or integration).

actor_type.description: The kind of actor that may bypass.

bypass_mode.description: Scope of the bypass: always, pull_request only, or exempt.

conditions.description: Conditions. Accepts only `ref_name` — organization-level condition keys 422 on the repository-rulesets endpoint, so they are rejected at authoring time rather than mid-sync.

ref_name.description: Patterns the ruleset applies to, as include/exclude name globs.

include.description: Glob-ish name patterns the ruleset applies to.

exclude.description: Glob-ish name patterns the ruleset must not apply to.

rules.description: The rules applied. `type` is required (catches obvious mistakes); the rest of each rule body passes through and GitHub validates it on write.

enabled.description: Create the `woodhouse/white-glove` check at all. If it is already a required status check in branch protection, disabling it here leaves PRs permanently blocked.

strictChecks.description: Checks that must report `success` explicitly: unlike ordinary checks they may not be skipped or neutral, and their absence holds the white-glove check pending rather than letting it pass.

ignoredChecks.description: Check runs excluded from evaluation entirely, by exact name. Useful for advisory-only checks (coverage reports, preview deployments).

gracePeriodSeconds.description: How long to wait for CI to register any check run on a commit before concluding there is none. During the grace period the check is held pending instead of passing on a commit nothing has tested; afterwards a commit with genuinely no checks passes, so docs-only repositories are not deadlocked. Raise it if CI is routinely slow to start.

gatekeeper.description: The `woodhouse/white-glove` consolidated check this schema configures.

enabled.description: Master switch. When false nothing is ever auto-approved; the rules below only apply while it is on.

owners.description: PR authors approved unconditionally (still subject to protectedPaths).

bots.description: PR authors approved only when they enabled auto-merge themselves.

allowedActors.description: PR authors whose pull requests are approved automatically, split by trust model: `owners` are approved unconditionally, `bots` only when they enabled auto-merge themselves.

protectedPaths.description: Refuse to auto-approve a PR that modifies any of these paths. Defaults cover the config files themselves: without it, any listed actor could self-approve a change that widens `allowedActors`, a privilege-escalation path.

autoApproval.description: Auto-approval of pull requests by trusted actors.
